literal_gloss: the flat world carried through space
definition: The novel's materially impossible world-frame: a disc carried by four elephants on Great A'Tuin, with an edge and its own rules of magic and causality.
cultural_caution: Discworld is a cosmology and setting, not a character node, a generic flat-world map, or proof that later series explanations are already fixed in this 1983 witness.

supports: The printed prologue establishes the disc, elephants, Great A'Tuin, Rimfall, and cosmological uncertainty.

literal_gloss: the eighth colour associated with magic
definition: The source names octarine as an eighth colour visibly associated with magic in the opening Ankh-Morpork conflagration and makes it the novel's title concept.
cultural_caution: The visual/magical association does not establish a transferable element, school, resource, or colour-coded power system.

citations.locator: Penguin 2022 ISBN 9781804990315, 'The Colour of Magic' p. 15
supports: The opening fire is described with magic's eighth colour, octarine.

literal_gloss: a magical practitioner; Rincewind's comic self-description uses a misspelling
definition: Wizardry is a learned but satirized social and institutional role, represented by Rincewind, Galder, Trymon, and Unseen University; Rincewind's 'wizzard' spelling signals the comic mismatch between title and competence.
cultural_caution: Do not turn the label into a uniform fantasy class, curriculum, or power ranking. Its parodic force and individual variation are essential.

citations.locator: Estate Rincewind page; The Colour of Magic introduction context
supports: Rincewind is first introduced in this novel and is characterized as an unusually unsuccessful Unseen University alumnus.

definition: The wizardly institution connected to Rincewind's background and to Galder Weatherwax and Trymon's novel-specific conflict over the Octavo/spell matter.
cultural_caution: This institution is a dimension, not a collective character, faction endpoint, generic magic academy, or evidence for later series governance.

supports: Rincewind's Unseen University background in the Discworld context.

literal_gloss: Twoflower's animated traveling chest made from magical pearwood
definition: Twoflower's formidable animated travel chest is an artifact/vehicle with apparent agency in the witness. It is kept as a dimensional term under the project's individual named-character rule.
cultural_caution: Do not promote the artifact to a character node or assume its later ownership, behavior, and appearance are all established by this single-novel pass.

citations.locator: Estate Luggage page; featured novel The Colour of Magic
supports: The Luggage's pearwood construction, mobility, and connection to Rincewind/this novel.

definition: The Wyrmberg episode uses dragons/wyrms as a source-specific, imagination-inflected fantasy convention around Liessa and Hrun; the kind remains a term while named human characters remain nodes.
cultural_caution: Do not treat this as a uniform monster species, mount category, or generic dragon-taming subsystem. The episode is overtly parodic.

citations.locator: The Colour of Magic, Penguin 2022 ISBN 9781804990315, 'The Lure of the Wyrm' printed witness
supports: The named section frames the novel's Wyrmberg/dragon episode.

canonical_term: The Octavo and its eight spells
literal_gloss: the dangerous spell-book and its constituent spells
definition: The Octavo/spell issue is a source-specific artifact and narrative pressure connecting Rincewind, Galder Weatherwax, and Trymon in the latter sections.
cultural_caution: It is not a character, a collectible spell deck, or a generic eight-school magic system. Scope is limited to its role in this novel.
